short: The pride of the Royal Navy for two decades, HMS Hood was a massive battlecruiser sunk by the Bismarck in 1941.
full:
Launched in 1918 and commissioned in 1920, HMS Hood was the largest warship in the world for over twenty years. As a battlecruiser, she was designed for exceptional speed and heavy firepower but sacrificed defensive armour compared to contemporary battleships. Throughout the interwar period, Hood served as a highly visible symbol of British imperial power during numerous flag-showing cruises.

In May 1941, Hood intercepted the German battleship Bismarck in the Denmark Strait. A plunging shell from Bismarck struck one of Hood's magazines, triggering a catastrophic explosion that tore the ship in half. She sank in minutes with the loss of all but three of her 1,418 crew, a profound psychological blow to the British public.
